# -*- coding: utf-8 -*- """ Blog post formatter with proper XSS protection. """ from html import escape # Predefined HTML template for a blog post. The placeholders {title} and {body} # will be replaced by the sanitized title and body strings. BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def format_post_content(post_title: str, post_body: str) -> str: """ Sanitize and format a blog post for safe HTML rendering. Parameters ---------- post_title : str The headline or title of the blog post. User-provided. post_body : str The full text content of the blog post. User-provided. Returns ------- str A complete HTML string with the title and body safely escaped, suitable for inclusion in a web page. Notes ----- * All user input is passed through html.escape, which converts special characters (e.g., <, >, &, ", ') into their HTML entity equivalents. * This approach protects against Cross‑Site Scripting (XSS) attacks (CWE-79) by ensuring that any embedded markup is rendered as plain text. * The function does not alter whitespace or line breaks in the body, preserving formatting. If you need to convert newlines to
tags or wrap paragraphs, additional logic can be added here. """ # Escape title and body to neutralize any HTML or script tags safe_title = escape(post_title, quote=True) safe_body = escape(post_body, quote=True) # Format the final HTML using the predefined template return BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body)
